summary: Late-stage development of linsitinib, an oral IGF-1R inhibitor for thyroid eye disease.
editor_note: The product bet is concrete: move a validated thyroid-eye-disease target from infusions to an oral small molecule. Sling has started the global Phase 3 ORBIT trial and received Fast Track designation, while its public pipeline distinguishes trial evidence from future commercial claims. Clinical efficacy, safety and regulatory review still decide whether convenience becomes a real treatment advantage.
why_featured: $123M Series C for an oral TED therapy
investors: Forbion, TPG Life Sciences Innovations, Sectoral Asset Management

product_evidence.claim: The pipeline page identifies linsitinib as an oral small-molecule IGF-1R inhibitor in Phase 3 development for thyroid eye disease.
The official financing announcement says the global Phase 3 ORBIT pivotal trial has begun and that the FDA granted Fast Track designation.

market_context.primary_user: Clinicians and patients managing moderate-to-severe active thyroid eye disease.
market_context.differentiation: Pursues a late-stage oral therapy against the same validated target addressed by currently infused or injected treatments.
market_context.why_now: The Series C finances a newly commenced global pivotal trial for a differentiated oral route.

risks.claim: Late-stage trial results and regulatory review may not confirm the efficacy, safety or convenience advantage suggested by earlier studies.
risks.basis: The inspected evidence reports Phase 2b/3 findings and a Phase 3 start; approval and commercial outcomes remain future events.
